dprCaveat: smallWebpKB is what a visitor's browser actually downloads ONLY when the computed <picture> 'sizes' slot times the page's devicePixelRatio is <= 480px. Measured on local-service's single-column mobile gallery card (real CSS width ~344px at a 390px viewport): a DPR-1 display (external monitor, some budget Android/older hardware) gets the 480w tile; a DPR-2 or DPR-3 display (most modern phones, including every current iPhone, and retina desktops) needs >480px of real resolution for that same 344px box and the browser correctly upgrades to the 960w tile instead — see local-service-summary.json, where 'after' full-page image bytes are identical (792577B) for the 390@DPR3 and 1440@DPR2 scenarios, and a separate DPR-1/DPR-2 spot check on the same file (in the session, not persisted as a script) showed 449191B at DPR-1 and 792577B at DPR-2/tablet-720@DPR-2. This is expected, correct <picture> behaviour, not a bug: a near-full-viewport-width photo on a high-DPR phone legitimately needs close to the same resolution as a modest desktop grid cell to stay sharp, and the whole point of Wave7 is refusing to trade that sharpness away just to hit a smaller byte count (see s54/s55). Multi-column contexts (Instagram grids, tablet/desktop 2-3 column galleries) and lower-DPR devices get the full ~80-90% saving in smallWebpKB; a full-bleed single-column mobile photo on a 2x/3x-DPR phone gets the ~43-65% saving in largeWebpKB instead (still real — that's the WebP format switch alone, over the original JPEG, at the same 960w resolution).
